description: A single-panel lower-triangular circle heatmap (corrplot style) showing the Pearson correlation coefficient matrix between 10 descriptors of low-density FeMnAlC steels: Mn, Al, C, Fe, VEC, Tm, ΔSmix, ΔHmix, Δχ and δ, printed in the same order along the top and the left edges. Every cell prints its numeric coefficient inside a coloured circle whose area and colour saturation scale with magnitude: dark blue for strong positive, white near zero, dark red for strong negative. A horizontal colour bar under the matrix spans -1 (dark red) through 0 (white) to a dark blue upper end, with printed ticks -1, -0.8, -0.6, -0.4, -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 (no tick label at the very top of the scale). The diagonal is unity throughout. The largest off-diagonal magnitudes are δ-C 0.98, δ-Δχ 0.98, Δχ-C 0.97, ΔHmix-δ -0.97, VEC-Al -0.94, ΔHmix-C -0.93 and Fe-Mn -0.9; Mn-Al, Mn-C and Al-C print 0. The figure identifies which descriptor pairs exceed the redundancy threshold used by the Pearson correlation filter.

subfigures.description: Lower-triangular 10x10 circle heatmap of Pearson correlation coefficients among Mn, Al, C, Fe, VEC, Tm, ΔSmix, ΔHmix, Δχ and δ; numbers printed in each circle, circle area and colour saturation proportional to |r| (blue positive, red negative, white ~0), with a -1 to ~0.9 diverging colour bar underneath labelled -1, -0.8, -0.6, -0.4, -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8.

observations.observation: The figure is a lower-triangular circle-formatted correlation matrix for exactly 10 descriptors; the row labels (top to bottom) and column labels (left to right) are Mn, Al, C, Fe, VEC, Tm, ΔSmix, ΔHmix, Δχ, δ.
All 10 diagonal cells print the value 1, shown as the largest dark-blue filled circles.
Printed coefficients for the δ row are Mn 0.04, Al 0.15, C 0.98, Fe -0.18, VEC -0.43, Tm 0.69, ΔSmix 0.57, ΔHmix -0.97 and Δχ 0.98.
Printed coefficients for the Δχ row are Mn 0.22, Al 0.04, C 0.97, Fe -0.29, VEC -0.35, Tm 0.71, ΔSmix 0.59 and ΔHmix -0.93.
Fe-Mn is the strongest negative element-pair correlation shown, printed as -0.9 (large red circle).
VEC-Al is printed -0.94 and ΔHmix-C is printed -0.93, both rendered as large dark-red circles.
Mn-Al, Mn-C and Al-C are all printed as 0, rendered as the smallest, nearly colourless circles.
The colour bar is a diverging scale with printed ticks -1, -0.8, -0.6, -0.4, -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8; the extreme upper end is dark blue and carries no printed tick value.

The caption states that the panel is a heatmap of the Pearson correlation coefficient matrix between the original 10 descriptors, and that a larger circle with deeper colour indicates a high level of correlation.
The caption states that the figure concerns feature selection to identify the most important features from the feature pool.

The citing text states that highly correlated descriptors were reduced with a Pearson correlation coefficient filter, defining highly correlated features as those with a correlation coefficient greater than 0.95.
The citing text states that Δχ and δ were eliminated from the model as redundant features, retaining only one of each highly correlated pair.
The citing text refers to the Pearson correlation coefficient map as being plotted in the lower left corner of Fig. 2, consistent with the lower-triangular layout actually shown.

measured_quantities: Pearson correlation coefficient r between descriptor pairs (unitless, range -1 to 1)
number of original descriptors in the feature pool (10)
